title:
Build your
ICP Brain
body:
A portfolio reviewer.
An interview coach.
Grounded in your own work.

title:
One body of context.
Two useful tools.
items: Find the most useful next edit for one project.
Practice one answer, get feedback, then try again.

title: See the full loop.
body:
A real review.
One coached answer.

title: The context does the work.
items: A shared lens for reviewing and practicing
footer: A simulated hiring perspective. Keep checking its judgment.

title: Open your workshop folder.
body:
In Code, choose
portfolio-brain
as your folder.
demoPurpose: Choose folder and inspect source files

title:
Start with what
you already know.
body:
Your homework is useful context.
You do not need to rewrite it.

title:
Your homework already
contains interview stories.
items: How you collaborate, make decisions, and want to improve.
People, projects, and moments that reveal how you work.
footer: Include relevant context. Leave out other people’s private details.

title: Check what Claude knows.
prompt:
Read the files in sources/. List what you could and could not read.

Summarize my experience, project contributions, strengths, and growth areas. Cite a source for each claim.

Flag missing or contradictory facts. Do not invent outcomes or infer my role from a team credit. Ask up to three questions that would improve your understanding.

title: Check what Claude understood.
body:
Check file access.
Correct your role
and missing facts.

title:
Give the reviewer
a point of view.
body: Your ICP is the person you want to hire you, described through their priorities.

title: Understand your target.
prompt:
Read targets/job-description.txt and only company notes relevant to that job.

Separate the employer’s stated requirements from your assumptions. Describe the likely portfolio reviewer and three reasons they might pass on work like mine. Cite evidence.

Compare those priorities with my project evidence. Identify one positioning tension: what could read as either a strength or a weakness? Turn it into three testable review rules.

title: Range needs a center.
items:
“I build brand systems.
The range is the proof.”
footer: For Decagon, test that argument against brand coherence, marketing work, and speed.

title: Make it reusable.
prompt:
Create ICP.md with my positioning, evidence, reviewer priorities, and unknowns. Keep shared candidate facts separate from each job’s lens.

Create .claude/skills/portfolio-review/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/interview-prep/SKILL.md with valid name and description frontmatter. Both read ICP.md and sources.

The reviewer gives three sourced edits and states its scope. Make interview prep adaptive: role-specific questions, follow-ups, no fixed question cap, varied retakes, and job switching. Update existing skills to these rules. Show the saved files and slash commands.

title: Find your saved context and skills.
body:
Open ICP.md.
Find both SKILL.md files.
Try the slash commands.
demoPurpose: Saved ICP, skill files and slash menu

title: Review one project.
prompt:
/portfolio-review sources/portfolio-project.pdf

Review this project using ICP.md and targets/job-description.txt. Give three prioritized edits.

For each edit, identify the specific sentence or visible detail, the hiring concern, and the proposed change. Cite the evidence.

State what you could actually read or see. Mark any new fact as needing my confirmation. Do not rewrite the whole project.

title: Ask it to show the evidence.
body:
Ask which sentence
or image supports
the recommendation.

title:
Use the same context
to tell a stronger story.
body:
Start with “Tell me about yourself.”
Get coaching. Try again.

title: Build the interview brief.
prompt:
/interview-prep brief targets/job-description.txt

Use ICP.md, my evidence, this job, and references/interview-question-bank.md.

Save outputs/INTERVIEW-BRIEF.md as a portable context pack: sourced role priorities, simulated ICP interviewer lens, supported stories, unknowns, and 8–12 seed questions. Seeds are not a limit.

Include intro → “Tell me about yourself” → coaching/retry, adaptive follow-ups, new questions, varied retakes, and job switching. Label inferences and question sources; never claim actual employer questions. Preserve a separate brief per job.

title: Move the brief into Claude.
body:
Share the full brief
in a regular Claude chat.
Your local files stay
in the Code project.
demoPurpose: Upload or paste the brief in regular Claude

title: Coach me after each answer.
prompt:
Use my brief. Wait until I say “Start the interview.” Give a short simulated interviewer intro, then ask “Tell me about yourself.” Wait; no example first.

After each answer, coach relevance, contribution, and evidence; suggest a supported example and invite a retry. Never invent facts.

Choose role-specific questions and follow-ups from my answers and the ICP lens. Keep going beyond the seeds. Support “continue,” “retry,” and “new round” with fresh questions after the opening. Switch jobs when I share a new description or brief.

title: “Tell me about yourself.”
body:
Hear the interviewer intro.
Answer aloud.
Get coaching. Retry.
demoPurpose: Interviewer intro → Tell me about yourself → coaching → retry

title:
Six pairs.
Two short rounds.
items: Partner A practices “Tell me about yourself,” hears coaching, and retries. Partner B listens.
Switch roles. Practice your own introduction for your target job.
footer: Use the final minute to save one improvement. Headphones; push-to-talk if the room is noisy.

title:
Does the retry
sound more like you?
items: It answers the question and connects to the job.
It names your decision, action, and contribution.
Its claims are true, supported, and in your voice.

title:
A reviewer you can reuse.
An answer you improved.
items: A specific next edit you understand
A portable setup for your next practice

title:
Keep going.
Try a new round.
Switch jobs.
body:
Say “continue,” “retry,” or “new round.”
For another job, share its description or brief.

title:
Questions?
Send me a note.
body: Happy to help you get unstuck.

title: Arrive ready to build.
items: Open a local folder in Claude Code and send a test prompt.
Save your resume, one portfolio project, homework, and one full job description.
Start a voice conversation in regular Claude. Bring headphones.
footer: Export Miro content into readable text or PDF. Bring only material you want the tools to use.

title:
Same person.
A more specific lens.
items: A senior design lead looking for craft, attribution, and a systems mind.
Brand system growth, marketing storytelling, and fast iteration with craft.
footer: The listing says “Brand Design Lead” and asks for 4–6 years. Treat seniority and fit as questions to investigate.
